line_items.reasoning: FY'25 adjusted EPS guidance was cut again to $19–$20, falling below the prior quarter's already-lowered range of $20–$21, driven by weaker industrial demand and a widened revenue-net-of-cost headwind.

Revenue came in weaker than the guided low single-digit growth, with the revenue net-of-cost headwind widening dramatically to $700M from the prior $100M estimate, and H2 Freight revenue now expected to decline slightly.

Federal Express adjusted operating profit grew 13% YoY on essentially flat revenue, with $146M in YoY operating income improvement, clearly demonstrating YoY margin expansion ahead of the reaffirmed guidance.

FedEx Freight operating profit fell $179M YoY in Q2 with average daily shipments down 8%, and H2 revenue is now expected to decline slightly — worse than the prior guidance of only a 'modest' margin decline.
No new information contradicts the $5.2B CapEx target; the company did not revise this figure, suggesting it remains on track as previously guided.
